title: infrastructure-weekly-update-2026-06-01
body:
Week: 2026-05-26 -> 2026-06-01
Owner: Aisha Patel (eng-infrastructure)
Purpose: weekly summary for GPU fleet, region capacity, and near-term capacity planning for Dedicated and Hosted customers. Includes standup notes, incident summaries, and action items.

1) Executive summary
- Fleet stable overall. Average GPU utilization across all production pools was 68% (hosted + dedicated) for the week. Slight uptick in peak latency tied to EU-west burst on Thu 2026-05-28.
- We validated the provisioning plan for onboarding two mid-market Dedicated customers (estimate: +72 A100-80GB equivalent GPU-days / peak). Request team approval to pre-warm 12 H100/80GB equiv. (see forecast below).
- One P2 incident (see Incident section) resulted in degraded throughput for ~45 minutes; root cause identified as CUDA driver regression on a small H100 sub-pool. Patch rolled within 90 minutes; follow-ups assigned.

2) Fleet health & metrics (last 7 days)
- Total GPUs in prod pools: 1,420 (mix: H100 64%, A100 36%)
- Avg utilization (prod): 68% (hosted: 72%, dedicated: 59%)
- Peak 95th percentile latency (text generation, 4k context): 320ms \u2014 +12% week over week, driven by EU-west burst on Thu
- Failed GPU nodes (hard failure): 6 (replacement completed for 5; 1 pending spare arrival)
- Scheduling backpressure periods: three short windows (max queue depth 220 requests) during Fri morning deployment rollouts

3) Regions & capacity notes
- US-west: Healthy. Sustained growth from a few Hosted customers; autoscaling added 60 GPUs mid-week without impacting latency.
- US-east: Minor throttling observed during nightly batch workloads; investigating placement of batch pools vs. interactive pools to avoid interference.
- EU-west: High contention Thu 05/28 due to simultaneous model rollouts from two partners. Triggered fallback to smaller-quant model variants for 18 minutes. Action: add a region-level admission control rule to smooth canary rollouts.
- APAC (Singapore): Low utilization but constrained by available H100 stock from the provider. We will continue using A100 spillover for lower-priority workloads.

4) Capacity planning & forecast (next 8 weeks)
- Near-term commitments: two Dedicated customers expected to go live between 2026-06-10 and 2026-06-24. Forecasted incremental peak demand: ~120 A100-eq GPUs.
- Procurement: Cloud provider quoted availability for additional H100 capacity with 2\u20133 week lead time. Recommendation: secure a 3-week reservation for 40 H100 equiv. as buffer for Dedicated ramp.
- Cost tradeoffs: pre-warming 12 H100 equiv. vs. on-demand burst \u2014 pre-warm reduces cold-starts by ~35% for our workload but increases committed spend. Finance asked for a conservative commit; propose a hybrid: reserve 20% of forecasted need, burst remainder.
- Long-run planning: schedule a capacity planning deep-dive (2 hrs) on 2026-06-08 with product and sales to finalize committed capacity and pricing tiers.

5) Incidents / Outages
- Incident (P2) \u2014 2026-05-28 14:12 -> 15:00 UTC: Throughput degradation in EU-west pool.
  - Symptom: 20% increase in error-rate and 30% drop in throughput for approx 45 minutes.
  - Root cause: regression in CUDA driver patch applied to a subset of H100 nodes during rolling maintenance; introduced a fallback behavior that caused kernel crashes under specific sequence lengths.
  - Mitigation: rolled back driver to previous stable; restarted affected runtime instances; queued requests routed to alternate region for high-priority customers.
  - Follow-ups: (a) Add driver patch gating and quick-smoke testing to rollout checklist (owner: Benji Rao, due 2026-06-03). (b) Improve canary sizing for driver updates to cover diverse sequence lengths (owner: Sofia Nguyen, due 2026-06-05).

6) Ongoing projects & status
- Autoscaling improvements (Miguel Torres): in-review PR that changes burst policy to prioritize latency-sensitive routes; expected to merge 2026-06-03.
- Regional admission control (Sofia Nguyen): prototype config for EU-west canary smoothing complete; rollout to staging 2026-06-02.
- GPU maintenance automation (Lena Volkova): playbook update for driver patches and health-checks; draft in Confluence, awaiting review.
- Rack/spare inventory (Benji Rao): spare H100 nodes shipment delayed; new ETA 2026-06-10. Temporary mitigation: increased node churn tolerance and adjusted drain policy.

7) Standup highlights (this week)
- Mon: Verified autoscaler regressions after last config change; hotfix queued.
- Tue: Customer spike from experiment infra caused short queues in US-west; autoscaler handled it but we logged heatmaps for further tuning.
- Wed: Capacity planning session with sales \u2014 preliminary sizing accepted, need to lock commit for procurement.
- Thu: Incident discussed above; after-action review scheduled.
- Fri: Oncall rotation handed off; no follow-up on-call incidents overnight.

8) Action items (owner / due date)
- Benji Rao: implement driver-gate testcases in CI for H100 kernels (due 2026-06-05)
- Sofia Nguyen: rollout regional admission control to staging and run load tests (due 2026-06-04)
- Miguel Torres: merge autoscaling PR and monitor next week (due 2026-06-03)
- Aisha Patel: run capacity deep-dive with Sales/Product (meeting 2026-06-08)
- Lena Volkova: update maintenance playbook and share for review (due 2026-06-06)

9) Risks & open questions
- Provider H100 supply risk: if lead times extend beyond 3 weeks we will need to fall back to larger A100 usage which increases per-token cost ~12% for some models.
- Dedicated customer SLAs: confirm whether sales are comfortable with staged capacity ramp (vs. guaranteed immediate capacity). Need Sales signoff.
- Autoscaler regressions: rolling conservative patches could cause slight latency increases; balance needed between stability and tail latency.

10) Notes / loose ideas
- Consider an "EU-canary credit" that holds small reserved capacity specifically for canaries to avoid impacting production traffic during rollouts.
- Explore short-lived spot pools in APAC for non-latency sensitive batch jobs to keep cost low while spare inventory arrives.

11) Meeting cadence & next steps
- Next infra weekly update: 2026-06-08
- Capacity deep-dive: 2026-06-08 15:00 UTC (invite sent to infra/product/sales)
- After-action review for 2026-05-28 incident: 2026-06-02 10:00 UTC (oncall + runtime + release eng)

Attachments / links referenced above: Confluence capacity plan, Jira INFRA-312 (driver gating), INFRA-325 (autoscaler).

-- End of update --
